Sergio / Monica —

We started seeing a ~60% drop in throughput across our production deployment beginning ~13:40 PDT. Token latency has stayed in-range, but requests are queueing and a subset of requests fail with 429/503. This started right after a config tweak on the KV cache we shipped yesterday to expand hot-prefix eviction windows.

Attached I uploaded a small log bundle from the frontline pods (brightbyte_log_bundle_20280620.tar.gz). Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side? This is blocking our batch jobs and several customer facing features. We're preparing a customer update; need visibility and ETA.

- Elena Park

Elena — thanks for the bundle and the heads-up. We’re triaging now. Initial read shows a burst of HOL (head-of-line) blocking on the primary KV namespace for BrightByte’s tenant, coinciding with an upswing in long-running prefix evictions. That can cause the scheduler to stall batching lanes and surface 429s when the in-flight window saturates.

Immediate plan:
- I’m escalating to runtime lead (Jonas) to validate whether the recent eviction-window change produced an eviction-amplification loop.
- Monica, can you coordinate a quick customer note? Need to set expectations for a 1–2 hour mitigation window.
- Elena, if you can keep streaming logs to the Drive link you provided, we’ll link them to the ticket.

I’ll follow up with an actionable rollback or fallback playbook in 20–30m.

- Sergio

On Tue, Jun 20, 2028 at 2:28 PM Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial read shows a burst of HOL blocking on the primary KV namespace ...

We dug into the runtime traces. Key findings:
- Eviction churn increased 8x after expanding the "hot-prefix retention" param at 09:00 PDT yesterday. The churn caused heavy KV metadata writes and lock contention on shard leaders.
- Batching lanes that rely on the primary prefix were waiting on KV lookups; other lanes backed up due to slot saturation.
- A small subset of requests hit our conservative fallback which returns 503s to avoid tail amplification — this explains the 503/429 mix.

Short-term mitigation I propose (safe, reversible):
1) Revert the retention param to previous value (this immediately reduces eviction rate).
2) Open a high-priority fallback routing: route new traffic to a read-only degraded variant with a warmer local prefix copy (3–5% quality delta).
3) Temporarily increase in-flight request window for BrightByte tenant by 15% to drain queues while retaining burst protection.

I’ll stage the revert and can execute a traffic steering plan in a safe window. Will post exact command and timestamps before taking action.

- Jonas
Runtime Lead
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-mitigation summary & playbook (fallback + safe rollback)

Team — final update after the staged mitigation executed this morning at 08:10 PDT:

What we changed
- 08:10: Reverted hot-prefix retention to prior value (config rollback).
- 08:17: Opened read-only fallback variant and routed 22% of BrightByte traffic to it.
- 08:25: Increased BrightByte in-flight window by 15% for 20 minutes to clear backlog.

Outcome
- Throughput recovered to ~95% of pre-incident within 28 minutes of starting mitigation.
- Error rate dropped from 6.4% -> 0.8% (primarily 503/429).
- No customer-facing data loss observed; quality delta on fallback variant measured ~3.1% for evaluated prompts.

Next steps (playbook attached: fallback-playbook-v1.md)
- Short-term: Keep fallback coverage at 20% for 2h and monitor KV eviction rate.
- Medium-term: Adjust eviction hysteresis algorithm for tenant-level churn (engineering RFC).
- Customer comms: Sergio to prepare a leadership-ready one-pager and Ben to finalize credit proposal.

Attachments: fallback-playbook-v1.md, rollback-flowchart.png

Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference
